sequenced-collections-concept-039.title: Use sequenced collections
sequenced-collections-concept-039.short: Access collection ends with a common API
sequenced-collections-concept-039.summary: SequencedCollection provides a common abstraction for collections with a defined encounter order and operations at both ends.
sequenced-collections-concept-039.why: It lets APIs work with ordered collections without depending on a specific implementation such as List or Deque.
sequenced-collections-concept-039.tips: Use reversed() when a reverse-order view is enough instead of copying elements.

text-blocks-concept-039.title: Use text blocks
text-blocks-concept-039.summary: Text blocks provide multiline string literals while reducing escaping and concatenation noise.
text-blocks-concept-039.why: They make embedded JSON, SQL, HTML, and other multiline text easier to read and maintain.
text-blocks-concept-039.tips: Watch incidental indentation and use ordinary strings when the value is naturally one line.

stream-map-multicode-039.title: Emit zero or more stream results
stream-map-multicode-039.summary: Stream.mapMulti lets one input emit zero, one, or many output elements through a consumer.
stream-map-multicode-039.why: It can express filtering and flattening without creating a temporary stream for every source element.
stream-map-multicode-039.tips: Keep the callback small and prefer flatMap when producing streams is already natural.

concurrent-modification-exception-039.title: Avoid structural changes during iteration
concurrent-modification-exception-039.short: Modify collections through supported iteration APIs
concurrent-modification-exception-039.summary: ConcurrentModificationException commonly appears when a fail-fast iterator detects unsupported structural modification of its collection.
concurrent-modification-exception-039.why: Changing the backing collection directly can invalidate the iterator's traversal state.
concurrent-modification-exception-039.tips: Use Iterator.remove, removeIf, or collect changes separately as appropriate.

date-time-exception-039.title: Handle invalid date-time values
date-time-exception-039.summary: DateTimeException is thrown when date-time values cannot represent a valid value, such as February 30.
date-time-exception-039.why: java.time types enforce their calendar and field ranges during construction and conversion.
date-time-exception-039.tips: Validate external input or parse with an appropriate formatter and error path.

generic-array-creation-error-039.title: Create an array of a parameterized type
generic-array-creation-error-039.short: Generic array creation is not allowed
generic-array-creation-error-039.summary: Java rejects direct creation of arrays whose component type is a non-reifiable parameterized type such as List<String>.
generic-array-creation-error-039.why: Arrays know their runtime component type while generic type arguments are erased, so the two type-safety models cannot be combined directly.
generic-array-creation-error-039.tips: Prefer a generic collection of collections instead of a generic array.

record-extra-field-error-039.title: Add an instance field to a record
record-extra-field-error-039.short: Records cannot declare extra instance fields
record-extra-field-error-039.summary: A record's instance state is defined by its record components, so additional instance fields are rejected.
record-extra-field-error-039.why: The record declaration is intended to describe its complete instance state explicitly.
record-extra-field-error-039.tips: Use record components for instance state or a normal class when extra mutable state is required.

serial-warning-039.title: Omit serialVersionUID
serial-warning-039.short: Serializable classes can declare a stable version ID
serial-warning-039.summary: With serial lint enabled, a Serializable class can warn when it does not declare serialVersionUID.
serial-warning-039.why: An automatically computed ID can change when class details change and make serialized data unexpectedly incompatible.
serial-warning-039.tips: Declare an intentional serialVersionUID when Java serialization compatibility matters.

optional-or-else-eager-trap-039.title: Compute an Optional fallback eagerly
optional-or-else-eager-trap-039.short: orElse evaluates its argument before the call
optional-or-else-eager-trap-039.summary: Optional.orElse receives an already evaluated fallback, so expensive fallback work runs even when the Optional contains a value.
optional-or-else-eager-trap-039.why: Normal Java argument evaluation occurs before orElse can inspect whether the fallback is needed.
optional-or-else-eager-trap-039.tips: Use orElseGet with a supplier when fallback creation is expensive or has side effects.

parallel-stream-shared-state-trap-039.title: Mutate shared state from a parallel stream
parallel-stream-shared-state-trap-039.short: Avoid unsynchronized side effects in parallel pipelines
parallel-stream-shared-state-trap-039.summary: Writing to a non-thread-safe shared collection from parallel stream operations can race and produce incorrect results.
parallel-stream-shared-state-trap-039.why: Parallel pipeline callbacks may execute concurrently on multiple threads.
parallel-stream-shared-state-trap-039.tips: Prefer reductions and collectors that let the stream framework combine results safely.
